verdict.rationale: Marlin lets the user set the research direction before execution through a brief exchange, and it builds a research plan from the topic, which gives some pre-run steering of scope. After that it runs without further human input; the only documented mid-run control is cancellation, which still consumes credits. missing for 10: documented controls for research depth or effort (e.g., run length or compute budget), mid-run steering or redirection beyond cancel, explicit scope parameters, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can steer the depth, effort, and scope of a research run before or while it executes

citations.quote: Sakana Marlin sharpens the direction of the investigation through a brief exchange with the user. Once the course is set, it works without further human input
Create a research plan based on the requested topic.
You can cancel at any time during execution, but please note that credits will still be consumed.
